title: Stance in Online Reviews
text:
Online reviews are often read as objective reports, yet most of them express a strong personal stance. A reviewer who writes 'the hotel was adequate' signals reluctance, while one who writes 'the hotel was superb' signals enthusiasm. Such adjectives carry far more meaning than their dictionary definitions suggest.

Writers can also show stance through intensifiers. Describing a meal as 'really quite good' suggests a more hesitant judgement than simply calling it 'good'. Readers who pay attention to these small choices often reach a clearer understanding of the reviewer's true opinion than the star rating alone would give.

According to the second paragraph, what does describing a meal as 'really quite good' suggest?

questions.text: What is the author's main point about star ratings?
options: They always reflect the writer's true opinion
They can hide the reviewer's real stance, which word choice may reveal

questions.text: Why might a reader trust the wording of a review more than its rating?
options: Ratings are always written by professionals
Wording reveals nuances of stance that a number alone may not show
Ratings are rarely given in online reviews

paragraph_translations: Las reseñas en línea suelen leerse como informes objetivos, pero la mayoría expresa una postura personal fuerte. Un reseñador que escribe 'the hotel was adequate' muestra reticencia, mientras que quien escribe 'the hotel was superb' muestra entusiasmo. Estos adjetivos transmiten mucho más significado que sus definiciones de diccionario.

Los escritores también muestran su postura mediante intensificadores. Describir una comida como 'really quite good' sugiere un juicio más vacilante que simplemente llamarla 'good'. Los lectores que prestan atención a estas pequeñas decisiones suelen comprender mejor la verdadera opinión del reseñador que la calificación con estrellas por sí sola.
